text: In 2005 archaeologists uncovered a large emptied grave underneath the chancel of the church at Hrísbrú where the altar would once have been. After the abandonment of the church, people had dug down through the floor to the grave below, most likely to extract the remains of the person in the grave and move them to new hallowed ground. The presence of a hole dug in the floor of the chancel ending in an emptied grave beneath the altar area parallels a description found in Egils Saga. It is impossible to say with certainty whether the grave uncovered by the archaeologists is the grave of Egil Skallagrimsson. We can only say that two independent data sets support the same scenario. Even without the saga, the archaeology speaks for the ritual reburial of an important person into a prestigious location below the altar. This treatment would have been reserved for a venerable ancestor that retained importance in the local historical tradition. According to Egils Saga, Egil was a respected ancestor and since Egil had been prime-signed (primo signatio) while serving in the army of the English king Aðalstan, he was suitable to be buried in hallowed earth.
